hints.title: Subtree Validation Properties
hints.text: A tree is a valid BST if the current value is strictly greater than the maximum in its left subtree and strictly less than the minimum in its right subtree.

hints.title: Bottom-Up Post-Order Traversal
hints.text: Process children first. Return four values from each node: whether the subtree is a BST, its total node count, its minimum key, and its maximum key.

hints.title: Size Aggregation on Valid Subtrees
hints.text: For an empty node, return true, count 0, infinity, and negative infinity. For a non-empty node, if both left and right subtrees are BSTs and the left max is less than node value and node value is less than right min, mark this node as a BST of size 1 plus left count plus right count. Otherwise, propagate the max count seen so far.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.notes: Single bottom-up traversal visits every node once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Validating each subtree independently from the top down requires quadratic O(N^2) time in the worst case.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Synthesizing BST properties bottom-up avoids redundant traversals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Traverse bottom-up and synthesize BST bounds and size in O(N) time.
